summary: This component renders a page displaying all blog posts from a specific series. It extracts the series name from the URL, looks up matching posts and their metadata, applies localization and styling, and displays them as a grid of cards with RSS feeds and a markdown export option.

explanations.36: This hook gives us access to the site's configuration object, which contains settings like the base URL (useful when the site isn't at the domain root).
explanations.37: We're removing any trailing slash from the base URL so we can safely combine it with the series path pattern—without this, we might accidentally create URLs with double slashes.
explanations.38: This function tries to match the current browser URL against a pattern like `/series/:slug`. If it matches, we extract the slug; if not, match is null and slug becomes undefined.
explanations.59: We're filtering the full list of blog posts down to only those that have a series name matching our URL slug (after normalizing both to the same format).
explanations.67: We grab the series name from the first post (which is guaranteed to have one after filtering), or fall back to the slug itself if there are no posts—this ensures we always have a string value to work with.
explanations.79: If the series has a brand color defined, we create a styles object with CSS custom properties that convert that color to different opacity levels for use in the hero banner; otherwise we leave styles undefined.
explanations.89: We're sorting posts newest-first by converting their date strings to timestamps and comparing them—the negative sign flips the order from oldest to newest.
explanations.95: The `translate` function is being called here to generate a page title that can be displayed in different languages, with the series name substituted into the template.
explanations.164: If we're on a translated version of the site (not the default locale), we also add an RSS feed link pointing to the source language version, which may have more articles since not everything is translated yet.
